Kole 265925 Rvw 24 of 2022 With Can 1 of 2025 With Can 1 of 2025 Shambhu Chandra Das
alias Shambhu Charan Das & Anr.
-Vs.-
Board of Trustees for the Post of Calcutta & Ors.

In Mat 1053 of 2021 Mr. Subir Sanyal, Mr. Amal Krishma Samanta, Mr. Arun Kumar Das, ... for the
appellants.
Mr. Prabal Mukherjee, Mr. Somnath Bose, .... For the Port Trust.
Dictated by Kausik Chanda J.
This is an application seeking review of the order dated November 24, 2021, passed by this Bench.

The relevant facts of the case have already been recorded in the said order, which is quoted below:
"It appears that the land of the appellants was acquired by the State by an acquisition proceeding and the Board of Trustees Kolkata Port Trust, Haldia Dock Complex (Port in short) was the requiring body in the said proceeding.

entities.text: Board of Trustees Kolkata Port Trust
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After acquisition of the land of the appellants, land loser certificates were issued by the project officer, Haldia Dock Complex in favour of the appellants.
The Port initiated an eviction proceeding under Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971 against the petitioners.

entities.text: Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: An order of eviction was passed by the Estate Officer.
The petitioners unsuccessfully challenged the said order before the appeal Court.
The revisional application filed against the order of the appeal Court was also dismissed by a learned Single Judge of this Court.

The appellants place reliance upon the order of the revisional Court wherein it has been observed that if there is any scheme for rehabilitation of the land losers in the aforementioned acquisition case, it is always open for the appellants to explore their rights under such scheme, in accordance with law.
The Port suggests that there is no scheme for rehabilitation of the land losers.

Before us,
the appellants could not produce any such scheme of rehabilitation.

In view of the aforesaid factual backdrop, in spite of being sympathetic to the appellants, we are of the opinion that there is no illegality in the order of the learned Single Judge since the appellants could not demonstrate any enforceable legal right in their favour.

The appeal being MAT 1053 of 2021 and the application being Shambhu Chandra Das Alias Shambhu ... vs Board Of Trustees For The Post Of ... on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46236881/
1 IA No. CAN 1 of 2021 stand dismissed without any order as to costs."

entities.text: Shambhu Chandra Das Alias Shambhu ... vs Board Of Trustees For The Post
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The review applicants seek reconsideration of the order on the ground that a scheme has been framed by the State Government under which the petitioners are entitled to rehabilitation by way of allotment of plot of land in their favour.
We have heard Mr. Sanyal, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the review applicants, on several occasions, as well as Mr. Mukherjee, learned Senior Advocate representing the Port Trust.

An affidavit was also called for from the State Government to clarify whether any rehabilitation scheme,
as claimed by the review applicants, exists.

After hearing the parties at length, we are constrained to hold that the review applicants have failed to produce or establish the existence of any scheme that confers upon the petitioners a right to rehabilitation.
The lands belonging to the petitioners were acquired for the purpose of the Haldia Dock Complex.
In lieu of such acquisition, the petitioners were granted compensation and also provided employment under the Port Trust.

We have already recorded in our order dated November 24, 2021 that in a prior revisional application challenging an eviction order passed by the Estate Officer under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971, a learned Judge of this Court had granted liberty to the petitioners to explore their rights in the event any such rehabilitation scheme exists.

entities.text: Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act, 1971
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The documents relied upon by Mr. Sanyal, which were disclosed in the affidavits filed by the State,
do not indicate the existence of any specific rehabilitation scheme applicable to the petitioners.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim rehabilitation on the basis of such documents is a matter that falls outside the scope of this review proceeding.
Upon careful consideration, we are of the view that no sufficient ground has been made out to warrant a review of the order dated November 24, 2021.
In view of the above, we are not inclined to entertain the present review application, and the same stands dismissed along with all connected applications.

However, the dismissal of this review application shall not preclude the petitioners from pursuing any remedy that may be available to them in law, including enforcement of their rights, if any, under any applicable rehabilitation scheme.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order be supplied to the parties, if applied for, as early as possible.

(Arijit Banerjee, J.) (Kaushik Chanda, J.)
